item.title: Algebraic dark solitons versus rogue waves in the massive Thirring model
item.description: arXiv:2611.27045v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We address the existence of algebraically decaying solitary waves on the nonzero wave background in the massive Thirring model (MTM) in laboratory coordinates. We find the precise condition of the spectral stability and instability of the nonzero wave background. In the case of instability, we distinguish modulational, side-band, and full-band instabilities and show that the rogue wave exists if and only if the nonzero wave background is modulationally unstable. For the other unstable cases and in the case of stability, we show that there exist exactly two algebraic dark solitons which correspond to the end points in the admissible range of the wave speed for the dark soliton propagation.
item.dc:creator: Zhen Zhao, Dmitry E. Pelinovsky

item.title: Transition processes of camphor particle motion in a three-chamber system
item.description: arXiv:2611.27478v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The motion of a camphor particle in a chamber with three circular regions was investigated through experiments and numerical simulations. Transitions between circular regions were analyzed as discrete stochastic processes. Experiments revealed the probabilistic transition of the camphor particle between regions, suggesting a tendency for the particle to undergo transitions in the same direction when transitions occur after a short dwell time. Numerical simulations using a stochastic mathematical model, where the geometry of the experimental system was incorporated through the boundary conditions, reproduced the tendency of transition of the camphor particle between three regions.
item.dc:creator: Ryoga Sato, Hiroaki Ito, Hiroyuki Kitahata

item.title: Simple Routes to Turing-Like Patterns
item.description: arXiv:2611.26814v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Spots, stripes, and networks recur in systems with very different microscopic dynamics, suggesting that the competing processes behind Turing-like patterns may be easy to realise. We ask whether local amplification coupled to suppression over a wider region can generate these geometries in simple systems beyond chemical reaction--diffusion models. We test this idea in two settings, a binary cellular automaton obtained by adding a distant neighbour count to Conway's Game of Life and a self-gravitating toy universe described by particle motion and two continuous fields. The automaton produces spots, stripes, and coexistence across its control plane, while a rule retaining only the two opposing counts produces islands, stripes, and holes. Directional correlations and intrinsic dimension identify the same region of orientational order. In the gravitational system, convergence increases local density while mass transport depletes the surroundings. The two-field and particle densities have a smoothed spatial correlation of $0.962$ at scale factor $a=1$ under the original force law, and strengthening its long-wavelength component drives both descriptions toward fewer dense condensations. Together, these results show how simple counting rules and redistribution of a conserved quantity can realise competing growth and suppression, providing two concrete routes by which Turing-like geometries can recur across different dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Zhan Zhao, Xiang-Ning Li, Wen-Wen Li, Ji-Chong Yang

item.title: Nonlinear stability of periodic waves in the Benjamin-Ono equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.27036v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct the Lyapunov functional for the periodic waves of the Benjamin-Ono equation based on the conservation of momentum, energy, and a higher-order energy, which exists due to integrability. Positivity of the second variation of the Lyapunov functional for perturbations in Sobolev space $H^1(\mathbb{R})$ is established by utilizing the basis properties of eigenfunctions of the linearized Benjamin-Ono equation in $L^2(\mathbb{R})$. Coercivity of the Lyapunov functional for co-periodic and multiple-periodic perturbations yields the nonlinear orbital stability of the periodic waves in the periodic domain.
item.dc:creator: Jinbing Chen, Colin Grant, Dmitry E. Pelinovsky

item.title: Asymptotic breathers in the Manakov system
item.description: arXiv:2610.26436v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct vector asymptotic Akhmediev breathers in the Manakov system, by matching generalized modulational-instability (gMI) eigenmodes to the preformation tails of the breather states. This branch-resolved matching provides analytical results linking the gMI-perturbation envelopes to the positions of the emerging breathers. Numerical simulations of the system with the focusing and defocusing nonlinearities corroborate the analytical predictions for each MI branch. We further develop the asymptotic theory for two-breather solutions generated by two gMI modes, linking their temporal separation to the input envelopes and interaction-induced shifts. Numerical simulations also reveal that breather patterns exhibit robustness in the presence of weak nonintegrable perturbations. These findings establish a framework relating experimentally controllable input modulations to the branch-selective formation and positioning of breathers in multicomponent nonlinear systems.
item.dc:creator: Liming Ling, Boris A. Malomed, Yan-Hong Qin, Jin-Peng Yang, Hao-Jun Yin, Li-Chen Zhao
